report:
FINAL LIST (as confirmed by the sisters; one list, kept here)

1 (C) — Fair share: her fair share of the house's value, not paying toward a discounted purchase for A.
2 (C) — B included: wants B to share in the value too, without deciding for her.
3 (A) — Secure home: wants a secure, independent home of her own; buying with her husband is how she sees getting there.
4 (A) — Fair to her sisters: wants it to feel fair to B and C; doesn't yet know what price or discount is fair.
5 (B) — Cash sooner: wants her share of the value sooner, to help start a dance studio.
6 (B) — Nothing settled early: uncomfortable with anything settled before all three agree.
7 (A) — Knowing it's affordable: wants to know she and her husband can pay without overreaching before committing.
8 (A, C, B — all confirmed) — Valuation is not a commitment: a jointly chosen, cost-shared independent valuation implies no commitment to buy or settle anything.

PROPOSED, NOT YET CONFIRMED (needs a reply next session): entry 9 (C, B) — "No automatic fallback: if O1 isn't affordable, no other option applies unless all three agree." C and B both raised this in their last replies; A hasn't been asked. Wording unconfirmed, so deliberately not recorded as settled.

STATUS
- Agreed by all three: only a jointly chosen independent valuer with shared cost. That is the sole point of agreement.
- Options: O1 (valuation at full value, shares paid at closing) is the option to test first — all three call it workable or possibly workable. O2 (A buys below market, A covers the entire shortfall to B and C) is second: A's closest fit, C's only if she's whole, B unsure of fair handling. O3 unsupported. O4 (open-market sale, three-way split) is C's fallback only.
- O1's open question: whether A and her husband can fund the amounts owed at closing (entry 7). If not, the fallback must be discussed and agreed by all three (proposed entry 9), not assumed.
- UNRESOLVED: the will's terms. No sister has seen them or knows who holds the document; all three say they'll ask the executor or their father's lawyer. Nothing may be treated as settled until the will is known and all three agree (entry 6).
- No legal decisions made, no money moved.

NEXT STEP: confirm entry 9's wording with all three, then have them jointly choose the surveyor and share costs. Report back before anything else is treated as agreed.
